summary: Turkey lets most European, Latin American and East Asian passport holders enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180, and runs an official eVisa portal (evisa.gov.tr) for nationalities that still need a visa, including a conditional eVisa for travelers holding a valid Schengen, US, UK or Irish visa.

stayWindow.text: Each visit may last up to 60 days, and all visits together may not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period. The 90/180 cap comes from the 2010 Russia–Türkiye agreement; Türkiye's 2013 decision raised the single-visit limit from 30 to 60 days.

defaultStayWindow.text: Türkiye counts the allowance across a rolling 180-day window: the MFA states the exemption as “90 days in any 180-day period” for nationality after nationality. Leaving and coming back does not start a fresh 90 days — days spent in the previous 180 still count against you. The MFA does not say whether the day you arrive and the day you leave are themselves counted, so we count both.

passportValidity.text: Turkey requires your passport to be valid for at least 60 days beyond the end of your visa, visa exemption or residence permit period; in practice at least 6 months' validity on arrival is recommended, and airlines may apply the stricter reading.

proofOfFunds.text: Tourist visa applicants must show sufficient and/or regular income; no fixed amount is published. Border officers may also ask any visitor about their means of support for the stay.

currencyLimits.text: Cash brought into Türkiye does not have to be declared, but customs officers may ask how much you carry and where it came from, and you must answer fully. Leaving Türkiye with more than TRY 25,000 or EUR 10,000 (or the equivalent in foreign currency) must be declared to customs on a cash declaration form; undeclared or misdeclared cash can be seized and fined.

notes: The UK FCDO says buying or exporting antiquities is illegal and can bring a fine and 5 to 12 years in prison. Some historical items sold in markets and antique shops are legal to buy in Türkiye but illegal to export, so confirm an item's status before you buy.

payments.text: No official source we could find describes how widely cards are accepted in Türkiye. Canada's travel advice says many small vendors, taxi drivers and rural businesses prefer cash, that card and ATM fraud occurs, and that you should exchange money only at reputable banks or official exchange offices.

safety.text: Tourist regions of Turkey are generally safe with visible policing. Avoid areas within 10 km of the Syrian border and any demonstrations, watch for street robbery and pickpocketing in Istanbul's main tourist areas, use registered, metered or app-booked taxis, and be wary of strangers who offer to take you to a restaurant or nightclub.

tips.text: Apply for the Turkish eVisa only at the official portal evisa.gov.tr. Look-alike third-party sites charge large markups on the official fee and sometimes deliver nothing.

The UK FCDO says buying or exporting antiquities is illegal, with fines and prison sentences of 5 to 12 years, and that some items legally sold within Türkiye still cannot be exported. Confirm an item's status before you buy it.
Keep some lira in cash: Canada says many small vendors, taxi drivers and rural businesses prefer cash. It also warns that card and ATM fraud occurs — use ATMs inside banks or shopping centres.

The UK FCDO says it is illegal to insult the Turkish nation or flag, and a criminal offence to insult the President or Atatürk — including online, wherever and whenever you posted. It also advises not photographing military or official installations, and says you must always carry photo ID such as your passport.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Turkey?
faq.answer: Under the visa exemption introduced in late 2023, US passport holders can visit Turkey visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Because the change is relatively recent, double-check your nationality's status on the official portal evisa.gov.tr shortly before travel.

faq.question: How much does the Turkish eVisa cost?
faq.answer: The fee depends on your nationality and is shown on evisa.gov.tr before you pay; the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs publishes no current fee table. Stays are 30 or 90 days depending on nationality; the ministry publishes no validity period.

faq.question: How long can EU citizens stay in Turkey without a visa?
faq.answer: Citizens of Germany, France, Spain, Italy and most other European countries can stay visa-free for up to 90 days within any 180-day period. The stay is not extendable as a tourist — longer stays require a short-term residence permit.

faq.question: How long must my passport be valid to enter Turkey?
faq.answer: Turkey asks for a passport valid at least 60 days beyond the end of your permitted stay, but at least 6 months' validity on arrival is recommended, since airlines and border officers often apply the stricter standard.

faq.question: What is Turkey's conditional eVisa?
faq.answer: Certain nationalities (including India, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Egyptians aged 15 to 45) can get a single-entry, 30-day Turkish eVisa only if they hold a valid visa or residence permit from a Schengen country, the US, the UK or Ireland and meet other conditions such as arriving with an approved carrier. Travelers who do not qualify must apply at a Turkish embassy. Eligibility is checked at evisa.gov.tr.
